input_contract: Implement the struct d_rope leaf/concat/flatten anchor with64 typed nodes, leaf length0–8 and maximum expanded length128. A rope is an ordered shared DAG: concatenating a root with itself must duplicate its logical bytes without mutating the shared leaf. Extend it with byte-index lookup and split, specifying allocation rollback and balancing separately. Implement two equal-byte-contract editing alternatives for a128-byte document: a gap buffer with explicit gap bounds and a piece table whose immutable original/add buffers are caller-owned and whose pieces are offset/length triples. Apply the same edit scripts to all three and a flat byte-list oracle. No Unicode scalar, grapheme or line-number equivalence is implied by byte offsets.
expected: Leaves ab and cd concatenate to abcd; concatenating that root with itself flattens to abcdabcd while the ab leaf remains ab. Capacity7 rejects an8-byte flatten without touching the output canary or written. An empty leaf returns root0.
independent_oracle: Generate edit traces length0–5 over insert empty/a/ab/NUL, delete zero/one/all and each boundary position, comparing byte sequences after every step. Check invalid positions and capacity exhaustion preserve state. Independently traverse the DAG to verify cached lengths, older-node edges and sharing; flatten must visit logical occurrences, not each unique node once. Construct left-deep concatenation to measure depth and compare balanced rebuild. The author anchor covers concat/flatten; split, balance, gap and piece implementations require their own submitted evidence and are not counted executed by that anchor.
